leads_to.evidence: Biology is the most common major among medical school applicants: biological sciences majors make up the majority of applicants and matriculants each year. First-year pay misses the many graduates who are still in school or working a gap year.

nearby_pair.evidence: Both are bachelor's programs open to new students. Keiser asks mainly for proof of high school graduation and admits nearly all applicants, and Florida Atlantic is a public university that admits freshmen.

school_matters.evidence: The usual entry science job, biological technician, needs only a bachelor's degree from any school. Graduates of the most selective schools earn only somewhat more than graduates of open schools, and the middle bands earn less than the open ones.

who_is_counted.evidence: The biggest general biology programs are at large public universities such as South Florida and Florida International, which admit traditional freshmen and transfers. None of the largest programs is online-only.

programs.evidence: MIT is one of the most selective schools in the country, and its biology graduates compete for the best research and biotech jobs in the Boston area.
